description: Firsthand triage of every Slither finding that touches prototype/vnext-kernel/contracts (see the vNext Kernel PR descriptions and W2S_SCANNER_TRIAGE_RECORD.md for the reachability argument behind each verdict). Keyed by "<check>|<sorted filename:line elements, de-duplicated across the per-entry-file recompilation crytic-compile's plain solc platform performs>" -- the same key generate-scanner-evidence.ts computes from a fresh --json run -- at the head named in keyedAt. Re-derived by Lane W2S under the CI-pinned toolchain from raw Slither runs on clean checkouts of the previous head (0faf7247) and the current one: every entry carries a provenance block naming its predecessor key and how identity was proven (UNCHANGED_FINDING_SAME_KEY / UNCHANGED_FINDING_RELOCATED / SEMANTICALLY_CHANGED_FINDING / NEW). generate-scanner-evidence.ts --validate fails if a fresh Slither run surfaces any finding whose key is not in this file, so an untriaged finding cannot silently disappear in a future change; a key that no longer matches any current finding is reported as stale and must be re-derived the same way, never re-keyed by line arithmetic alone.

reentrancy-events|prototype/vnext-kernel.rationale: deployVault's external calls before the event are genesisSalt (a STATICCALL to the immutable implementation, which cannot mutate state) and initialize(g, pqKey) on the clone address that Clones.cloneDeterministicWithImmutableArgs (an internal-library CREATE2) just produced in this same call. A brand-new contract with no prior code cannot reenter deployVault before it exists, and the only code at that address is the kernel's own initialize, which makes no external call (it validates g and the pqKey exhibit by keccak256 and length comparison, writes genesis state and emits). VaultDeployed is emitted after the call with no state left for a reentrant call to exploit: the factory holds no mutable state at all (VaultKernelFactoryPrototype.sol's own header: its authority closure is EMPTY). Re-adjudicated by Lane W2S because the construct changed BEFORE W2, in #187 (SD-6/SD-7, I-COMMITMENT-EXHIBITED-AT-ADMISSION): pqKey became a forwarded parameter of deployVault and initialize. The exhibit is a satisfiability witness, adds no external call and changes nothing in the reentrancy argument.

timestamp|prototype/vnext-kernel/contrac.rationale: cancelRecovery's only clock read is the _recoveryIsLive() gate at VaultKernelPrototype.sol:1254, adjudicated under the timestamp entry keyed :742,:743. The comparison Slither prints for this function, recovery.challengesUsed >= CHALLENGE_LIMIT (:1255), has no timestamp-derived operand: challengesUsed is written only by the += 1 in this function, the carry-forward in initiateRecovery and the whole-struct delete in executeRecovery (I-RECOVERY-CHALLENGE-EPOCH). It is reported because the timestamp detector evaluates data dependency in NODE context: after the _recoveryIsLive() internal call, whose return value depends on block.timestamp and on the recovery struct, the node-context dependency set of the recovery storage reference includes block.timestamp (probed with the pinned Slither's is_dependent: node-context true, function-context false, W2S_SCANNER_TRIAGE_RECORD.md section 5.2); the identical comparison at e6964aeb, gated by the raw recovery.active byte, produced no report. What the clock decides here is WHETHER a credential challenge is admitted: while live (t < expiresAt) the challenge consumes one budget unit and clears request authority; once expired it is refused with NoRecovery before any nonce or budget is touched (test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B3 'challenge' probes; mutant M-K9-expired-request-still-challengeable). Bounded skew (0 s on post-merge L1, ~15 s forward-only PoW-era, 1,800 s OP-Stack sequencer drift) can move that instant by seconds against a 14-day window and can neither refund nor exceed the budget, so it hands the credential no capability beyond the bounded challenge that architecture section 22 D1 already prices (I-VETO-BOUND).

provenance.changeNote: Introduced by c182db10 (W2): the gate if (!recovery.active) became if (!_recoveryIsLive()), which taints the function's later nodes in Slither's node-context dependency. Not present at 0faf7247 or e6964aeb.

timestamp|prototype/vnext-kernel/contrac.rationale: executeRecovery gates on block.timestamp < r.executableAt (TooEarly; RECOVERY_DELAY = 7 days) and, CHANGED BY W2 (SD-9e, Recovery Amendment section 3), on block.timestamp >= r.expiresAt (Expired; RECOVERY_EXPIRY = 14 days): the half-open window [executableAt, expiresAt) that makes execution consistent with _recoveryIsLive(). At expiresAt-1 execution, both cancellations and the migration block all hold; at expiresAt and expiresAt+1 execution reverts Expired, both cancellations revert NoRecovery consuming no nonce and no budget, migration binds, and a fresh initiation is admitted with its own full delay (test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B4 and G3, each probe mined at its asserted instant). Re-adjudicated in Lane W2S rather than carried forward: the only difference the change makes to the timestamp argument is that the last authorised instant moved from expiresAt to expiresAt-1, removing the one-second window in which the pre-W2 kernel executed a request every other consumer already treated as expired. Validator discretion is bounded: post-merge L1 timestamps are fixed per 12-second slot (no proposer discretion; the only lever is inclusion), PoW-era skew was at most ~15 s and forward-only (a lagging timestamp cost the miner difficulty and was corrected by the next honest block), and OP-Stack L2 sequencer drift is bounded at 1,800 s relative to the L1 origin -- at most 0.3% of RECOVERY_DELAY and 0.15% of RECOVERY_EXPIRY. Skew moves both bounds of every principal's window together, reads no signature, quorum or possession check, and therefore cannot execute an unmatured or expired request, cannot bypass the quorum that alone creates an active request (initiateRecovery), and cannot reset the challenge epoch, whose only reset is this function's own delete recovery after a successful, authorised execution. Mutant M-K9-expiry-inclusive-off-by-one (> here, <= in the predicate) is killed by the B-series boundary property (test/W2RecoveryLifecycleMutations.test.ts).

timestamp|prototype/vnext-kernel/contrac.rationale: _recoveryIsLive() IS I-RECOVERY-EFFECTIVE-LIVENESS (Recovery Amendment section 3): a request holds authority on the HALF-OPEN window [executableAt, expiresAt), so active && block.timestamp < recovery.expiresAt is the one deliberate clock read that every recovery-lifecycle decision consults -- initiateRecovery's live-overwrite refusal, cancelRecovery, cancelRecoveryByQuorum and bindMigration; executeRecovery mirrors it with >= expiresAt. Adjudicated independently in Lane W2S (W2S_SCANNER_TRIAGE_RECORD.md section 5), not inherited from the older timestamp entries. (1) The predicate decides only WHETHER an already-authorised act lands, never WHO is authorised: no signature, quorum or possession check reads the clock, so no authority cut in AUTHORITY.md section 4 moves with it. (2) Every consumer applies the same inequality, so there is no block in which the request is executable but not cancellable, or cancellable but not executable; test/W2RecoveryLifecycle.test.ts B1-B3 pins all five consumers at expiresAt-1 (live: execution succeeds, both cancellations succeed, migration is blocked, initiation is refused as overwrite), expiresAt and expiresAt+1 (expired: Expired / NoRecovery with nothing consumed / migration binds / fresh initiation admitted), and G3 pins the three instants as consecutive blocks of one world. (3) Validator discretion is bounded: post-merge L1 timestamps are fixed per 12-second slot (no proposer discretion; the only lever is inclusion), PoW-era skew was at most ~15 s and forward-only, and OP-Stack L2 sequencer drift is bounded at 1,800 s relative to the L1 origin -- at most 0.15% of RECOVERY_EXPIRY (14 days) and 0.3% of RECOVERY_DELAY (7 days); a forward skew can only make a request expire EARLY, shrinking every principal's window together, never extend it. (4) Consequently skew cannot refund the challenge epoch (challengesUsed is written only by the += 1 in cancelRecovery, the carry-forward in initiateRecovery and the whole-struct delete in executeRecovery), cannot bypass the quorum (only initiateRecovery creates an active request), cannot execute an expired request (t >= expiresAt reverts, and expiry is defined in the same clock the request was created in), cannot overwrite a live request (initiateRecovery reverts BadState while live; a fresh request over an EXPIRED one is by design not an overwrite, and the quorum could in any case have cancelled its own live request) and cannot lower any cut. Mutants M-K9-expiry-inclusive-off-by-one, M-K9-expired-request-still-challengeable, M-K9-expired-request-still-quorum-cancellable, M-K9-expired-request-blocks-migration, M-K9-expired-request-blocks-initiation, M-K9-live-overwrite-allowed and M-K9-expiry-refunds-budget are all killed (test/W2RecoveryLifecycleMutations.test.ts).
